messages:
alicia: Quick heads-up — noticed our A100 preemptible capacity in us-east-1 dipped ~40% this morning and evictions spiked. Thinking about running a multi-SKU sensitivity experiment (A100, A10G, T4, L4) with packing policy changes and a lightweight 'burst lane' for short jobs. Thoughts?

ben: Ugh, saw the same. Evictions clustered around the 03:00 maintenance windows. Also curious if checkpoint traffic was amplifying the networking noise.

sandeep: Confirmed — a few long-running trainers hit rsync/ssh SIGPIPEs while being migrated. Network burstiness + simultaneous checkpointing looks like a multiplier for failures.

maria: From perf tests, A10G gives ~70% of A100 throughput but with higher tail variance on longer contexts (seq=1024+). T4/L4 are fine for short convo-style loads. We should tag by tail-latency tolerance.

alicia: Proposed plan: 1) split fleet into steady (A100) + opportunistic (A10G/T4/L4) with labels for tail-latency tolerance; 2) change packing scoring to prefer colocating same PCI/NIC topology to reduce cross-host NIC pressure; 3) add a 90-120s 'graceful-drain' token on preemptions so checkpoint hooks get time to finish (and back-pressure to the scheduler).

ryan: For (2) what does the scoring function look like? maybe: score = 0.6*free_slots + 0.4*sku_affinity ? We should also factor in recent eviction rate.

sandeep: I like: score = free_slots - eviction_risk + sku_affinity_bonus. eviction_risk is a sliding window metric based on past 24h interruptions + region maintenance calendar spikes.

ops-bot: deploy plan queued by @alicia — canary packing tweak rolled to 10% of new allocations for 48h. :eyes:

ben: Also recommend throttling checkpoint rsyncs with a token bucket to cap egress bursts. Sample config to try on canary agents:
```
checkpoint:
  rsync_rate_limit: 50mbps
  burst: 200mb
  retry_policy: exponential(5s, 60s)
```

maria: Let's run a 72h cost-sensitivity experiment across us-east-1 and us-west-2 with a 70/30 steady/opportunistic split and measure p50/p90/p95 latency, eviction count, successful checkpoint rate, and cost-per-token. Include model classes (seq len buckets) in the telemetry.

alicia: Canary started just now. I'll wire the metrics dashboard and share a link later. If you want your workload included, ping me and I'll add the tag. Good call on the rsync rate limit — that should lower correlated network incidents. :rocket:
